title: A complex four-point method for the evaluation of ohmic and faradaic losses within a redox flow battery single-cell
author: Mazur, Mrlik, et al.

steps.title: Prepare platinum wire pseudo‑references
steps.instruction: Cut four high‑purity platinum wires (0.25 mm diameter); designate two as SM+ and SM− for electrolyte inlet placement and two as SP+ and SP− for attachment to composite plates.

steps.title: Fabricate membrane sealing with embedded wires
steps.instruction: Hot‑press each platinum wire between two thermoplastic elastomeric sheets to fix its position; create an outer sealing sheet with a small hole for electrolyte contact and an inner sealing sheet that prevents wire‑membrane contact and sets a 0.2 mm gap between wire and membrane.

steps.title: Install pseudo‑reference wires in cell
steps.instruction: Place SM+ and SM− in the electrolyte inlet channels on both sides of the membrane, positioning them near the graphite felt electrodes without touching them; ensure the wires are sealed by the membrane sealing assembly.

steps.title: Attach plate‑reference wires to composite plates
steps.instruction: Bond SP+ and SP− to the inner side of the carbon composite plates (PPG86) using PTFE adhesive tape (Gore).

steps.title: Assemble flow‑battery single cell
steps.instruction: Layer the cell components in order: PVC cell body, elastomeric gaskets, carbon composite plate with SP wire, graphite felt electrode (20 cm² active area, compressed 25 % of original thickness), PFSA cation‑exchange membrane (Fumatech), second graphite felt electrode, second composite plate with SP wire; insert the membrane sealing assemblies containing SM wires; verify no wire contacts the electrodes.

steps.title: Prepare vanadium electrolyte
steps.instruction: Mix commercial electrolyte to obtain 1.6 mol dm⁻³ total vanadium ions with a 1:1 M ratio of V³⁺:V⁴⁺, 2 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄, and 0.3 % H₃PO₄ (GfE); bubble nitrogen gas through the negative electrolyte to suppress V(II) oxidation.

steps.title: Set flow and temperature conditions
steps.instruction: Pump electrolyte through the cell at 40 cm³ min⁻¹ (≈27 cm min⁻¹ linear velocity) and place the assembled cell in a temperature‑controlled box set to 20 °C.

steps.title: Connect potentiostat and configure measurement
steps.instruction: Link the cell to a Biologic EC‑LAB VSP‑126 potentiostat/galvanostat/FRA equipped with a 4 A current booster; connect current collectors and all four platinum wires to the appropriate channels.

steps.title: Perform electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
steps.instruction: Run EIS with a 5 mV AC amplitude over a frequency range of 200 kHz to 50 mHz for the full cell, the positive half‑cell (using SM+), and the negative half‑cell (using SM−); save spectra for later fitting.

steps.title: Conduct load‑curve measurements
steps.instruction: Apply a linearly increasing current scan from 0 to +200 mA cm⁻² (charging) and from 0 to –200 mA cm⁻² (discharging) at a rate of 1 mA cm⁻² s⁻¹; record the cell voltage versus current density for full‑cell and each half‑cell.

steps.title: Analyze EIS data
steps.instruction: Fit the recorded spectra with the equivalent circuit shown in Fig. 4 using EC‑Lab software; extract the intercept (R_IN) as the ohmic resistance and the low‑frequency semicircle diameter (R_CT) as the charge‑transfer resistance; note the use of a constant phase element (CPE) for the double‑layer capacitance.

steps.title: Calculate area‑specific resistances from load curves
steps.instruction: Determine the slope of the charge and discharge U‑j curves for each configuration; the slope equals the area‑specific resistance under load.

steps.title: Repeat measurements at 50 % state‑of‑charge
steps.instruction: Charge the cell with constant current until the electrolyte reaches +50 % SOC (defined by equimolar V⁴⁺:V⁵⁺ in the catholyte and V²⁺:V³⁺ in the anolyte); repeat EIS and load‑curve measurements as in previous steps.

steps.title: Compare and report results
steps.instruction: Summarize the extracted ohmic and faradaic resistances for full‑cell, each electrode, and the membrane; verify that the summed half‑cell resistances agree with full‑cell values; note that the platinum wires did not affect coulombic efficiency or capacity.
